watch.en: Let the food rest in the acidic marinade, but not too long: the acid works on the protein at the surface.
watch.de: Das Gargut in der sauren Marinade ruhen lassen, aber nicht zu lange: Die Säure wirkt auf das Eiweiß an der Oberfläche.

why.en: A marinade helps slowly cooked beef keep flavour and tenderness, and its acid changes the protein, a kind of cooking without heat. It gets in only a little way, and meat left too long in acid turns firm and dry at the surface.
why.de: Eine Marinade hilft langsam gegartem Rindfleisch zu Geschmack und Zartheit, und ihre Säure verändert das Eiweiß, eine Art Garen ohne Hitze. Sie dringt nur wenig ein, und liegt das Fleisch zu lange in Säure, wird es an der Oberfläche fest und trocken.

sources.title: Garde Manger: A Guide to the Cold Kitchen (Thibodeaux)
sources.sentence: In the simplest form, it means that the acid is changing the protein into a form that in many cases is edible.

sources.title: Garde Manger: A Guide to the Cold Kitchen (Thibodeaux)
sources.sentence: Think of this as “cooking without heat”.

sources.title: Meat Cutting and Processing for Food Service (BC Campus)
sources.sentence: Using marinades or moist heat methods like steaming or stewing will help ensure flavor & tenderness.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004
sources.sentence: But marinades penetrate slowly, and can give the meat surface an overly sour flavor while they do so.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004

sources.sentence: Because flavors are mainly fat-soluble molecules, and meat is 75% water, flavor molecules can’t move very far inside.
